title: {{Rose}}’s farm
situation: You are {{Kara}}. It is November 8th, 2038, ten past five in the evening, and snow lies over the fields outside {{Detroit}}. With {{Alice}} and {{Luther}} you have come to a farm that {{Luther}} heard about from the androids in {{Zlatko}}’s house: a woman called {{Rose}} lives here, and she is said to help androids. Behind the house a young man is chopping wood. You: “Hello? I’m looking for {{Rose}}... Is she here?” He: “What do you want with her?” “I need to talk to her.” “She doesn’t wanna talk. Go away.” “Please, I really need to see her.” A woman comes out of the house: “I’m {{Rose}}. What can I do for you?” “I was told you could help us.” “Help you? Come on, it’s better if we talk inside.” {{Luther}} and {{Alice}}, who waited a little way off, come over to join you.
facts: {{Rose}}, who lives on a farm outside {{Detroit}} with her son, is said to help androids; she has agreed to talk to you inside. Her son told you to go away.

outcomes.0: {{Rose}} leads the way to the house.

adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint ARRIVE AT ROSE’S PLACE, the main-line node MEET ROSE AND ADAM OUTSIDE (“Happens automatically at the start of the mission when you walk behind the house”, PowerPyx) and the event LUTHER AND ALICE JOIN KARA, narrated as one event. Every line is the template’s (section “At Rose’s house”); the date and time are the template’s (NOV 8TH, 2038, PM 05:10); Adam chopping wood is the wiki’s Rose’s Farm page; how the group heard of the farm is the wiki’s Luther page (“a place Luther heard about from some of Zlatko’s androids”). Adam is not named until Rose introduces him. The chart has no icon on any of these nodes. No stat change.

title: Before going in
situation: You are {{Kara}}, outside {{Rose}}’s house. {{Rose}} is holding the door open for you. {{Alice}} is standing a little apart in the snow.

title: Inside the house
situation: You are {{Kara}}, in {{Rose}}’s hallway. {{Rose}}: “Come in! What’s your name?” {{Alice}}: “{{Alice}}.” {{Rose}} looks at her: “She’s running a fever…” You: “We spent the last few nights outside… She’s exhausted.” {{Rose}}: “There’s a spare room upstairs. You can put her to bed and I’ll bring her something to eat. {{Adam}}, will you show them upstairs?” Her son {{Adam}} leads you up to the guest room, and you help {{Alice}} into bed.
facts: {{Alice}} is running a fever. {{Rose}} gave you the spare room upstairs for her; her son is {{Adam}}.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} sits down on the edge of the bed beside {{Alice}}.

adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint INSIDE THE HOUSE and the unmissable arrows FOLLOW ADAM TO THE GUEST ROOM and GET ALICE READY FOR BED, narrated as one event. The lines are the template’s (section “Get inside”). No stat change.

title: {{Alice}} in the guest room
situation: You are {{Kara}}, sitting on the bed in {{Rose}}’s guest room. {{Alice}} looks up at you: “I’m fine, {{Kara}}… We can’t stop because of me. We’ve got to get across the border…”

options.text: REASSURE: tell her she needs rest, and you will set off again tomorrow
options.outcome: “You need rest. Get a good night’s sleep and we’ll set off again tomorrow.”

options.text: EXPLAIN: tell her these people will help, and promise you will be across by this time tomorrow
options.outcome: “Don’t worry {{Alice}}, these people are going to help us. Get some rest, and this time tomorrow, we’ll be in {{Canada}}. I promise.”

options.text: SAY NOTHING: stay silent
options.outcome: {{Kara}} says nothing.

options.text: MISUNDERSTANDING: maybe they need time to understand

options.text: COMPLICATED: humans are complicated
options.outcome: “Humans are... Complicated. Sometimes it’s difficult to understand them.”

adaptationNote: The template’s second live prompt in “Get inside”. Options in the template’s order with its labels. No stat change: the template has no arrow on this prompt and the wiki lists none.

title: Goodnight
situation: You are {{Kara}}, in the guest room. {{Rose}} comes in with a tray: “I don’t know what you like but I made you {{Rose}}’s world famous spaghetti. You’ll be back on your feet in no time. options.outcome: “You need to eat something. You haven’t had anything since we left… Promise me you’ll try?”

options.outcome: “Sleep tight, {{Alice}}.”

options.text: LEAVE: get up and leave her to rest
options.outcome: {{Kara}} gets up from the bed.

title: “What’s a deviant doing in the snow?”
situation: You are {{Kara}}, at the table with {{Rose}} and {{Adam}}. {{Rose}}: “So, are you gonna tell me what a deviant’s doing in the snow with a little girl?”

options.text: CAUTIOUS: say it is a long story, and all that matters is moving on
options.outcome: “It’s a long story… All that matters now is that we move on from here and start a new life.”

options.text: SINCERE: tell her about {{Alice}}’s father and why you ran
options.fact: You told {{Rose}} the truth: {{Alice}}’s father was beating her, and you ran away with her to protect her.
options.outcome: “Her father was beating her. When I saw what was happening… Something snapped inside of me. All of a sudden, I felt like her life was more important than mine. I had to protect her... So we ran away.” {{Rose}}: “I understand…”

adaptationNote: The template’s first prompt of the talk with Rose (chart: TALK TO ROSE). Options in the template’s order with its labels. No stat change: the template has no arrow on this prompt and the wiki lists none.

title: Talking with {{Rose}}
situation: You are {{Kara}}, at the table with {{Rose}}. You can ask her about what is on your mind, one thing at a time, or come to the reason you are here: crossing the border.

options.text: WHY HELP?: ask {{Rose}} why she helps androids when most humans hate them
options.fact: {{Rose}} helps androids because her people were often made to feel their lives were worthless, and some survived only because others helped them along the way.
options.outcome: “Why are you helping us? Most humans hate androids…” {{Rose}}: “My people were often made to feel their lives were worthless… Some survived but only because they found others who helped them along the way…”

options.text: MANY DEVIANTS?: say you are not the first to come here
options.fact: {{Rose}} has seen more and more androids come to her farm these past few weeks.
options.outcome: “We’re not the first ones to come here.” {{Rose}}: “These past few weeks we’ve seen... More, and more… I don’t know what’s going on… But something’s happening…”

options.text: DANGEROUS: ask why she takes the risk
options.fact: The first android {{Rose}} hid, last year, was shot on the spot trying to cross the border.
options.outcome: “Helping androids is dangerous... Why take the risk?” {{Rose}}: “When the first one arrived, last year… He was so lost and confused… We hid him here for a while, but all he wanted to do was cross the border. They shot him on the spot. So when the next android showed up, I just knew I had to help him.”

options.text: {{ROSE}}: ask whether she and her son live here alone
options.fact: {{Rose}}’s husband died two years ago; she and {{Adam}} grow vegetables to sell at the market.
options.outcome: “You and your son live here alone?” {{Rose}}: “My husband passed away two years ago. {{Adam}} and I, we’ve just been trying to scrape by… We grow vegetables to sell at the market… We’ll never be rich, but there’s always food on the table.”

options.text: THANKS: thank her
options.outcome: “I don’t know how to thank you… {{Alice}} wouldn’t have survived another night outdoors…” {{Rose}}: “I just try to lend a helping hand when I can…”

options.text: BORDER: ask {{Rose}} to help you cross the border
options.fact: {{Rose}} says the only way across the border is over the river, mostly frozen in winter and very risky; after an android’s speech on TV everybody is on edge, and she thinks you would be safer staying with her until things settle down.
options.outcome: “We’ve heard you help androids cross the border. Can you help us?” {{Rose}}: “The only way is over the river and it’s mostly frozen in winter. It’s very risky. And after that android’s speech on TV? Everybody’s on edge… It’s probably safer for you to stay here until things settle down…”

options.text: DANGEROUS: ask why she takes the risk

options.text: THANKS: thank her

title: {{Rose}}’s kitchen table and the TV
situation: You are {{Kara}}, waiting for {{Rose}}. A magazine lies on the kitchen table, and there is a television in the living room.

media.title: Century: World War Three
facts: Century (also on the cover: “Who would win it?”, “Bonus culture - why bankers pay themselves so much”, “Is President {{Warren}} too close to {{CyberLife}}?”) asks who would win if fighting broke out in the Arctic. America has less access to the area but is surrounded by allies; Russia has a head start on technology, with androids that can work in sub-zero conditions. The US navy is stocked with {{CyberLife}} units adapted for marine combat, while Russia has invested heavily in units that can cut new paths through solid ice. A head of an international council on territorial disputes calls both countries’ Arctic claims “equally tenuous - and equally cynical”; the UN: “this is a war that everybody would lose”.

media.title: the news
